subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this ten-table shared durable-state foundation in the canonical `openclaw.sqlite` database before the related RFC and recovery design have maintainer sponsorship?
rationale: The patch is intentionally an internal foundation, but it establishes persistent cross-owner records and shared-handle semantics that later code and upgrades must support; tests can validate implementation mechanics but cannot choose the permanent core ownership model.

options.title: Pause for RFC sponsorship
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until maintainers accept or narrow the residual durable-core boundary in the linked RFC.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow foundation
options.body: Approve only the specific shared facts and schema lifecycle contract required for a named follow-on recovery path, then request focused upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep ownership-specific state only
options.body: Reject the generic shared layer and require each recovery or delivery gap to remain in the existing task, flow, subagent, session, or queue owner.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until maintainers accept or narrow the residual durable-core boundary in the linked RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor is the only concrete owner identified in the supplied series context and can incorporate a maintainer decision into the proposed stack; the actual accept/narrow/reject decision remains with OpenClaw maintainers.
